answer: FAIL_F6. Three load-bearing decisions ship with NO options table in the PR body or any in-tree evidence row: (D1) hand-emit 173 evidence files vs a generator (`omc msr backfill --pr <list>`) — given 74 of 173 files share the same skeleton with only ~24-39 lines of mostly templated content (per pr-17-meta files[*].additions distribution), a generator path is the canonical-fit alternative and is not named; (D2) one mega-PR with a single squash commit for the entire 9-PR retroactive wave vs per-PR-batch granular commits (one commit per reviewed PR, or per-facet) — chosen path destroys the ability to revert evidence for a single bad PR without dragging the other 8 down; (D3) requiring every facet to ship both r1 AND r2 even when r1 is a substantive PASS (the r2 files are uniformly 39 lines of confirmatory shape vs r1's 24-90 lines of substance) vs allowing a no-op r2 schema (single field {round:2, status:'r1_stands'}) that would eliminate ~74 × 39 ≈ 2,886 lines of boilerplate. The PR body's 'Naming justification' section is strong (names every artifact family with one-line rationale, satisfying the naming-justification feedback note) and 'Validation' lists 3 concrete tools (`jq empty`, `git diff --check`, direct cargo). But neither section, nor any in-tree evidence file, surfaces the three F6 alternatives above. The retroactive nature (review evidence for already-merged PRs) further weakens F6 because the alternatives table CANNOT change the underlying PR outcomes — but it CAN change the cost/correctness of the next backfill wave, which is the live decision F6 is being asked to protect.
alternatives_considered: ==DECISION 1: HOW TO EMIT 173 EVIDENCE FILES (PR chose hand-emit; F6 supplies competitors)==

A: Hand-emit all 173 files (THE SELECTED PATH). Cost: ~7,639 added lines, every file an independent edit, error surface = 173 × per-file-typo-rate; reviewer cannot detect a structural-drift between sibling files without diffing pairs by hand. Benefit: zero new tooling, no generator to maintain.

B [Linus-style — minimal generator]: `omc msr backfill --pr <N> --facets F1..F9 --skeleton evidence/templates/r1.json` — a 50-100 LOC shell or Rust binary that reads a per-PR YAML manifest (verdict, key_claims, alternatives) and emits the skeleton JSON. Per-PR YAML is ~5x smaller than per-facet JSON because skeleton fields are factored out. Cost: 1 new tool; benefit: 173 files become 9 YAML manifests + 1 generator, drift between sibling files is structurally impossible.

C [hyperscaler-style — schema-driven codegen]: Define an `evidence/schemas/multispectrum-r1.schema.json` JSON-schema, generate per-PR-per-facet JSON via `jq -n` with a parameterized template, and CI-validate every emitted file against the schema. Aligns with the project's own [Doc-coverage enforced] feedback discipline. Cost: schema authoring + jq pipeline (~30 LOC); benefit: schema becomes the canonical evidence contract, generator output is provably conformant, future facets (A1..A7) auto-pick-up the same shape.

D [hybrid — template + per-facet enrichment]: Author 1 r1 skeleton per PR using the generator (B), then hand-author ONLY the F-facet rows that have substantive findings (e.g. pr-5 had a re-dispatch, pr-3 had real F1 findings) — the rest are stamped as confirmatory. Compromise between (A) full-manual and (B) full-generator that mirrors the spectrum-lens-subagent doctrine (only spend brain on facets that have something to say).
==DECISION 2: COMMIT GRANULARITY (PR chose 1 squash commit for 9 PRs; F6 supplies)==

A: Single mega-PR with 1 squash commit covering evidence for 9 PRs (THE SELECTED PATH). Cost: cannot revert evidence for one bad PR without dragging the other 8; bisect noise; reviewer cannot timebox to 'review evidence for PR #5 only' because the commit shows all 173 files at once.

B [Linus-style — per-PR commit, single PR]: Same PR but 9 commits, one per reviewed PR (commit subjects: 'evidence: pr-1 multispectrum r1+r2+synthesis'). Reviewer can `git show <sha>` per PR; revert granularity = per-PR; bisect resolution = per-PR. Cost: 9 commits instead of 1; benefit: surgical revertability.
C [Linus-style — per-PR-per-round commit]: 9 × 3 = 27 commits (r1, r2, synthesis per reviewed PR). Cost: more commits; benefit: revert a bad round without losing the PR's other rounds.

D [hyperscaler-style — N separate PRs]: 9 separate PRs, one per reviewed PR, all targeting `dev` and merged in sequence. Cost: 9 PR-create-merge cycles, more CI runs; benefit: each PR is independently revertable, the audit-chain event lands per-PR (matching the audit-chain's own per-PR granularity).
==DECISION 3: r2 SCHEMA POLICY (PR chose full r2 file per facet; F6 supplies)==

A: Require a full ~39-line r2 JSON file for every facet of every PR (THE SELECTED PATH). pr-17-meta confirms 74 r2 files at 34-39 lines each = ~2,800 lines of mostly-confirmatory boilerplate. Cost: 100% of the boilerplate is non-load-bearing for PASS-r1 cases; reviewer fatigue; obscures the few r2 files (e.g. pr-5-F5-r3) that DO carry substance.

B [Linus-style — no-op r2 schema]: Allow r2 to be {`reviewer_id`, `round`:2, `facet`, `status`:'r1_stands', `notes`:''} when r1 already produced a substantive verdict. ~10 lines instead of 39. Eliminates ~2,100 lines of boilerplate from THIS PR alone and from every future backfill wave. Cost: schema must distinguish substantive-r2 from no-op-r2 (a single enum field); benefit: future reviewers can grep for `status:'r2_overrides'` to find the rounds that matter.

C [Linus-style — omit r2 entirely when r1 is conclusive]: Make r2 file presence itself the signal — if no r2 file exists, r1 stood. Cost: tooling that scans for 'is the review complete' must accept absence-as-pass; benefit: eliminates the file entirely. Risk: harder to distinguish 'r1 stood' from 'r2 was never run' — argues for B over C.

D [hyperscaler-style — r2 as a synthesis-roll-up only]: Drop per-facet r2 files; replace with a single per-PR `synthesis.json` (which the PR already ships) that contains a `rounds_seen` array. Cost: lose per-facet round-trace; benefit: 74 r2 files collapse to 0.

recommendation: PASS_WITH_RESERVATIONS for THIS PR (retroactive, merged, evidence is in-tree and well-named). BLOCK posture for the NEXT backfill wave: require (1) `omc msr backfill` generator (or equivalent jq-from-schema pipeline) before any wave >50 files; (2) per-PR commits within a single PR OR per-PR separate PRs (author's choice, but not 1-squash-for-9); (3) a no-op-r2 schema or an explicit ADR that justifies why every facet must ship a substantive r2. linus_style_alternative: Hand-write the 9 synthesis files (the load-bearing artifacts), generate the 162 per-facet round files from a 50-LOC jq script reading 9 per-PR YAML manifests. Total author effort drops from 173-file-edit to 9-yaml-edit + 1-script-author. Drift between sibling files becomes structurally impossible. The synthesis files (which carry actual cross-facet judgment) remain hand-authored because that IS the load-bearing reasoning surface.
hyperscaler_style_alternative: Schema-driven evidence pipeline: evidence/schemas/{r1,r2,synthesis}.schema.json + a `cargo run -p oya-msr-evidence-emitter -- --pr-manifest evidence/manifests/pr-N.yaml` binary that emits all 19 files per PR (9 r1 + 9 r2 + 1 synthesis), CI-validates schema conformance via a new `lean-a-evidence-schema` lane, and rejects PRs whose evidence does not pass schema. Aligns with the project's [Doc-coverage enforced] and [Quality/Performance/Scalability bar] feedback. Cost: ~200 LOC + 1 CI lane; benefit: future facets (A1..A7 own-policy-adherence) auto-pick-up the same emission pipeline, evidence drift becomes a build error.
